prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Русский / Tiếng Việt · Diacritics (language ru).
Grid: 3 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Термин" · longest unbreakable word 134px · one-line width 134px
  col 2: header "Tiếng Việt" · longest unbreakable word 36px · one-line width 111px
  col 3: header "Описание" · longest unbreakable word 90px · one-line width 615px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 568px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 567px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A Russian–Vietnamese terminology table pairs technical terms with translations and explanations.","reading":"Readers scan the Russian term and its Vietnamese equivalent together, then read across the row for the explanation. Wrapped text should remain clearly associated with its row.","groups":["Columns 1 and 2 form the terminology pair: Russian terms and their Vietnamese equivalents.","Column 3 provides explanatory prose for each pair."],"keep_intact":["Russian terms, including the 134px unbreakable term","Individual Vietnamese words and diacritics","Individual words in the descriptions"],"may_wrap":["Vietnamese multiword equivalents at word boundaries","Descriptions at natural word boundaries; their longer prose will generally set the row height"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [155, 132, 280] · table 568×214px · row heights [33, 73, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [155, 90, 322] · table 568×214px · row heights [33, 73, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [190, 112, 265] · table 568×214px · row heights [33, 73, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
